## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: multi-factory shared-branch caveat — fixed `fa-tokens.json` asset vs the documented "one branch, one asset per factory" topology**

`statePublish.asset` exists precisely so multiple factories can share one `factory-data` branch (`assetName` → `<factory>-state.json`), but the tokens probe is a single fixed asset:

```js
var FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET = 'fa-tokens.json';   // data/<asset> on the data
```

If a second factory ever publishes to the same repo + branch, both ticks would read the SAME `data/fa-tokens.json`. Token keys are repo-global (`pr-N`), so factory A's leg rows would silently attach to factory B's cards → wrong spend numbers on the board, with "—" replaced by plausible-looking data (worse than a miss).

The ticket explicitly pins the fixed name to the producer design, so this does not block. Suggested follow-up (can land with the producer or when a second factory actually shares a branch): honor a `statePublish.tokensAsset` override with `fa-tokens.json` as default — one line here (`(cfg && cfg.tokensAsset) || FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`), and the multi-factory story stays symmetric with `assetName`.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: third copy of the gh Contents-probe pattern — consider a shared `contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec)` helper**

`fetchTokensFromBranch` duplicates the probe/decode/parse sequence that now exists in ~5 places across this module:

```js
var raw = execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/data/' +
    FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET + '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) +
    ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
return tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(raw));
```

Same shape lives in `fetchPreviousState` (content fetch), `publishFactoryState` (sha probe), and twice in `updateHistory` (sha probe + content read) — differing only in path, ref, and post-parse validation. Extracting a tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec) {
    try {
        return execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/' + path +
            '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) + ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
    } catch (e) { return null; }
}
```

would leave each call site as `tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))` and keep the transport (whitelist-gh-first, in-shell base64 decode) pinned in one place for the next mirror-the-pattern change.

Not blocking — the mirror of `fetchPreviousState` is explicit and the duplication is mechanical.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: make the tokens source visible on the publish log line**

Both token sources degrade silently by design (correct — tokens are decorative), but once this ships an operator cannot tell from a tick log whether the board's numbers came from the local file, the branch, or nothing at all. A persistent miss (mis-typed `tag`, revoked Contents read scope, producer writing to a different repo) is indistinguishable from "producer hasn't landed yet" — both render "—" forever, with zero signal.

The publish path already logs provenance lines:

```js
console.log('  📡 factory state published → ' + spUrl);
```

Consider one sibling line, e.g. `🪙 tokens: N legs (branch|local|none)` — it makes the fallback path observable in the same place, costs nothing per tick, and would have made the gh-781 owner report ("no tokens visible") diagnosable in one glance. Avoid a per-miss `console.warn`: pre-producer the branch 404s every tick and the log would just fill with noise.

Not blocking — purely operability polish.

# pr-783: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)

## Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 783
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/783
- **Title**: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-781` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T06:58:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T07:09:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #783._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: multi-factory shared-branch caveat — fixed `fa-tokens.json` asset vs the documented "one branch, one asset per factory" topology**

`statePublish.asset` exists precisely so multiple factories can share one `factory-data` branch (`assetName` → `<factory>-state.json`), but the tokens probe is a single fixed asset:

```js
var FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET = 'fa-tokens.json';   // data/<asset> on the data
```

If a second factory ever publishes to the same repo + branch, both ticks would read the SAME `data/fa-tokens.json`. Token keys are repo-global (`pr-N`), so factory A's leg rows would silently attach to factory B's cards → wrong spend numbers on the board, with "—" replaced by plausible-looking data (worse than a miss).

The ticket explicitly pins the fixed name to the producer design, so this does not block. Suggested follow-up (can land with the producer or when a second factory actually shares a branch): honor a `statePublish.tokensAsset` override with `fa-tokens.json` as default — one line here (`(cfg && cfg.tokensAsset) || FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`), and the multi-factory story stays symmetric with `assetName`.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: third copy of the gh Contents-probe pattern — consider a shared `contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec)` helper**

`fetchTokensFromBranch` duplicates the probe/decode/parse sequence that now exists in ~5 places across this module:

```js
var raw = execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/data/' +
    FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET + '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) +
    ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
return tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(raw));
```

Same shape lives in `fetchPreviousState` (content fetch), `publishFactoryState` (sha probe), and twice in `updateHistory` (sha probe + content read) — differing only in path, ref, and post-parse validation. Extracting a tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec) {
    try {
        return execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/' + path +
            '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) + ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
    } catch (e) { return null; }
}
```

would leave each call site as `tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))` and keep the transport (whitelist-gh-first, in-shell base64 decode) pinned in one place for the next mirror-the-pattern change.

Not blocking — the mirror of `fetchPreviousState` is explicit and the duplication is mechanical.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: make the tokens source visible on the publish log line**

Both token sources degrade silently by design (correct — tokens are decorative), but once this ships an operator cannot tell from a tick log whether the board's numbers came from the local file, the branch, or nothing at all. A persistent miss (mis-typed `tag`, revoked Contents read scope, producer writing to a different repo) is indistinguishable from "producer hasn't landed yet" — both render "—" forever, with zero signal.

The publish path already logs provenance lines:

```js
console.log('  📡 factory state published → ' + spUrl);
```

Consider one sibling line, e.g. `🪙 tokens: N legs (branch|local|none)` — it makes the fallback path observable in the same place, costs nothing per tick, and would have made the gh-781 owner report ("no tokens visible") diagnosable in one glance. Avoid a per-miss `console.warn`: pre-producer the branch 404s every tick and the log would just fill with noise.

Not blocking — purely operability polish.

---

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: gh-781 lands exactly what the ticket scopes — `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch` mirrors `fetchPreviousState` (one gh Contents probe, any miss → `null`), the `readTokensFile || fetchTokensFromBranch` precedence is pinned and tested, and the `tokensMapOf` extraction is a semantics-preserving refactor. Verified locally: `run_factoryState.json` 66/0, `run_smAgent.json` 336/0, full `run_all.json` 1793 passed / 0 failed (matches the PR claim), snapshot schema stays 2; AC1–AC4 each have a dedicated test. No blocking or important findings; security surface is unchanged (repo/tag are config-controlled, gh-first whitelist respected, board-side `esc()` covers the new row fields).

- Tokens source (local/branch/none) is invisible in the tick log — a one-line `🪙 tokens: N legs (<source>)` next to the 📡 publish line would make degradation diagnosable

1. Merge as-is — the three suggestions are follow-up polish, not rework

# pr-783: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)

## Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash

   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 783
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/783
- **Title**: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-781` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T06:58:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T07:09:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

`statePublish.asset` exists precisely so multiple factories can share one `factory-data` branch (`assetName` → `<factory>-state.json`), but the tokens probe is a single fixed asset:

If a second factory ever publishes to the same repo + branch, both ticks would read the SAME `data/fa-tokens.json`. Token keys are repo-global (`pr-N`), so factory A's leg rows would silently attach to factory B's cards → wrong spend numbers on the board, with "—" replaced by plausible-looking data (worse than a miss).

The ticket explicitly pins the fixed name to the producer design, so this does not block. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):

would leave each call site as `tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))` and keep the transport (whitelist-gh-first, in-shell base64 decode) pinned in one place for the next mirror-the-pattern change.

The test harness supports `captureConsole: true` → `sm.capturedLogs`. So for Thread 3's log line test, I can pass `captureConsole: true` to `publishTick`'s opts (it goes through `makeSmAgent(opts)`), then assert `run.sm.capturedLogs.some(...)` matches `🪙 tokens: 2 legs (branch)` etc.

Wait — does the statePublish block's console.log get captured? The mock comment says the mock shadows the module-scope console for every loadModule'd module that receives smMocks (smAgent...). Yes.

Now, plan the TDD work:

### Fix 1 (Thread 1): `statePublish.tokensAsset` override
- RED: test in test_factoryState.js — `fetchTokensFromBranch('o/r', { tag: 'factory-data', tokensAsset: 'factoryB-tokens.json' }, exec)` probes `data/factoryB-tokens.json`; default unchanged when absent.
- GREEN: `var asset = (cfg && cfg.tokensAsset) || FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET;` in fetchTokensFromBranch.

### Fix 2 (Thread 2): shared `contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec)` helper
- RED: hmm, this is a refactor — existing tests already pin exact command strings for fetchPreviousState, fetchTokensFromBranch, updateHistory. A refactor test: export `contentsOf` and pin its behavior (miss → null, content returned). The "test that first reproduces the issue" — for a pure refactor, the existing suite IS the regression net. TDD rule R1 says never change production code without a test that first reproduces it — for refactors, the characterization tests (existing exact-command assertions) cover it. But to be faithful to TDD, I'll add a small `contentsOf` suite that pins the helper's contract (returns decoded content on success; null on any transport failure; exact command shape), export it, then refactor the call sites and keep everything green.
- GREEN: add `contentsOf`, refactor `fetchPreviousState`, `fetchTokensFromBranch`, `updateHistory` content read to use it.

Wait — should `contentsOf` swallow errors? The suggested helper returns null on transport failure. In `updateHistory`, the content read is `JSON.parse(execOut(...) || '{}')` inside try/catch — contentsOf returning null → `null || '{}'` → '{}' → snaps=[]. Good.

In `fetchPreviousState`: `JSON.parse(contentsOf(...))` — if null → JSON.parse(null) → null → `(parsed && parsed.lanes)` → null. But wait, currently the try/catch wraps JSON.parse — if contentsOf returns null, JSON.parse(null) returns null without throwing, and the function returns null via the guard. Semantics preserved.

Actually hold on — should `fetchPreviousState` keep its own try/catch? With contentsOf swallowing transport errors, JSON.parse(null)→null→guard returns null. JSON.parse of garbage throws — still inside the outer try/catch → null. So keep the outer try/catch for the parse. Fine.

For `fetchTokensFromBranch`: `tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))` — contentsOf null → JSON.parse(null) → null → tokensMapOf(null) → null. Garbage → JSON.parse throws → outer catch → null. Good.

For the sha probes (`publishFactoryState`, `updateHistory` sha probe): the thread only suggests contentsOf for the content+base64 pattern. The sha probes use `--jq .sha` without base64 decode and have distinct semantics ("Not Found" string check). I could add a parallel `shaOf` helper... The review explicitly says "differing only in path, ref, and post-parse validation" and proposes contentsOf. I'll keep the sha probes as-is to stay surgical — the fix is about the content-fetch duplication. Hmm, but "check same pattern across codebase" (F3). The sha probes ARE the same transport. But changing `publishFactoryState`'s sha probe has subtle semantics (keeps res object handling, "Not Found" check, empty→'' instead of null). The suggestion scoped contentsOf to content fetches. I'll do exactly the suggested helper for content fetches (3 sites). That fully resolves the thread. Note the sha probe in `publishFactoryState` uses `exec(...)` directly with a different result handling, and `updateHistory`'s sha probe uses execOut. I'll leave both.

Actually, let me reconsider — thread 2's title: "third copy of the gh Contents-probe pattern — consider a shared contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec) helper" and it says "would leave each call site as tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))". The scope is content fetches. Good — 3 sites.

### Fix 3 (Thread 3): tokens provenance log line
- RED: test in test_smAgent.js — publishTick with captureConsole + branch tokens → logs contain `🪙 tokens: 2 legs (branch)`; local file → `(local)`; neither → `(none)`.

Wait, with no tokens at all, would it log `🪙 tokens: 0 legs (none)`? The thread suggests `🪙 tokens: N legs (branch|local|none)` as a single sibling line — always logged (persistent signal, not per-miss warn). So yes: `0 legs (none)` when nothing found. That's the operator signal.

- GREEN: in smAgent.js, restructure the tokens read to track source, compute leg count, log after the 📡 line.

Leg count computation: sum of array lengths across map values. I'll add a helper `tokensLegCount` in factoryState.js? Or inline in smAgent. The board-side card rows come from normalizeTokens... The count of legs = total rows in the map. Let me add a tiny exported helper `tokensRowCount(map)` in factoryState — testable, keeps smAgent thin. Name: `tokensLegCount`. Hmm, let me look at what reads naturally: `🪙 tokens: N legs (source)`. I'll add:

```js
/**
 * Total leg rows across a tokens map ('pr-N'/'issue-N' → array rows) —
 * the N in the tick's 🪙 provenance line. Null/empty → 0.
 */
function tokensLegCount(map) {
    var n = 0;
    Object.keys(map || {}).forEach(function (k) {
        n += Array.isArray(map[k]) ? map[k].length : 0;
    });
    return n;
}
```

Export it. Test it in test_factoryState.js.

In smAgent.js:

```js
var spTokens = factoryStateModule.readTokensFile(
    (spCfg && spCfg.tokensFile) ||
        factoryStateModule.DEFAULT_TOKENS_FILE,
    function (p) { return file_read({ path: p });
var spTokensSrc = spTokens ? 'local' : 'none';
if (!spTokens) {
    spTokens = factoryStateModule.fetchTokensFromBranch(spFull, spCfg,
        function (a) { return cli_execute_command(a); });
    if (spTokens) spTokensSrc = 'branch';
}
```

And after `console.log('  📡 factory state published → ' + spUrl);`:

```js
// 🪙 provenance (rework gh-783): which source fed card.tokens this tick —
// a persistent miss (bad tag, revoked scope) is otherwise indistinguishable
// from "producer hasn't landed yet". One line, always: no per-miss noise.
console.log('  🪙 tokens: ' +
    factoryStateModule.tokensLegCount(spTokens) + ' legs (' +
    spTokensSrc + ');
```

Where exactly? After the 📡 publish line, before history update. The thread says "one sibling line" next to the 📡 publish line. 

Now — one question: is the log line inside the `try` block? Yes, inside `try { ... } catch (ePub)`. If tokensLegCount throws... it won't (null-safe). OK.

Also should the log happen even when publish succeeds — yes.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

- **Title**: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-781` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T06:58:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T07:09:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

If a second factory ever publishes to the same repo + branch, both ticks would read the SAME `data/fa-tokens.json`. The ticket explicitly pins the fixed name to the producer design, so this does not block. ### Fix 1 (Thread 1): `statePublish.tokensAsset` override
- RED: test in test_factoryState.js — `fetchTokensFromBranch('o/r', { tag: 'factory-data', tokensAsset: 'factoryB-tokens.json' }, exec)` probes `data/factoryB-tokens.json`; default unchanged when absent.

### Fix 2 (Thread 2): shared `contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec)` helper
- RED: hmm, this is a refactor — existing tests already pin exact command strings for fetchPreviousState, fetchTokensFromBranch, updateHistory. A refactor test: export `contentsOf` and pin its behavior (miss → null, content returned). The "test that first reproduces the issue" — for a pure refactor, the existing suite IS the regression net. TDD rule R1 says never change production code without a test that first reproduces it — for refactors, the characterization tests (existing exact-command assertions) cover it. But to be faithful to TDD, I'll add a small `contentsOf` suite that pins the helper's contract (returns decoded content on success; null on any transport failure; exact command shape), export it, then refactor the call sites and keep everything green.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 783
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/783
- **Title**: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-781` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T06:58:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T07:09:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# pr-783: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)

## Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 783
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/783
- **Title**: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-781` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T06:58:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T07:09:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #783._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: multi-factory shared-branch caveat — fixed `fa-tokens.json` asset vs the documented "one branch, one asset per factory" topology**

`statePublish.asset` exists precisely so multiple factories can share one `factory-data` branch (`assetName` → `<factory>-state.json`), but the tokens probe is a single fixed asset:

```js
var FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET = 'fa-tokens.json';   // data/<asset> on the data
```

If a second factory ever publishes to the same repo + branch, both ticks would read the SAME `data/fa-tokens.json`. Token keys are repo-global (`pr-N`), so factory A's leg rows would silently attach to factory B's cards → wrong spend numbers on the board, with "—" replaced by plausible-looking data (worse than a miss).

The ticket explicitly pins the fixed name to the producer design, so this does not block. Suggested follow-up (can land with the producer or when a second factory actually shares a branch): honor a `statePublish.tokensAsset` override with `fa-tokens.json` as default — one line here (`(cfg && cfg.tokensAsset) || FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`), and the multi-factory story stays symmetric with `assetName`.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: third copy of the gh Contents-probe pattern — consider a shared `contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec)` helper**

`fetchTokensFromBranch` duplicates the probe/decode/parse sequence that now exists in ~5 places across this module:

```js
var raw = execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/data/' +
    FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET + '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) +
    ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
return tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(raw));
```

Same shape lives in `fetchPreviousState` (content fetch), `publishFactoryState` (sha probe), and twice in `updateHistory` (sha probe + content read) — differing only in path, ref, and post-parse validation. Extracting a tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function contentsOf(repo, path, cfg, exec) {
    try {
        return execOut(exec, 'gh api repos/' + repo + '/contents/' + path +
            '?ref=' + tagOf(cfg) + ' --jq .content | base64 -d');
    } catch (e) { return null; }
}
```

would leave each call site as `tokensMapOf(JSON.parse(contentsOf(...)))` and keep the transport (whitelist-gh-first, in-shell base64 decode) pinned in one place for the next mirror-the-pattern change.

Not blocking — the mirror of `fetchPreviousState` is explicit and the duplication is mechanical.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: make the tokens source visible on the publish log line**

Both token sources degrade silently by design (correct — tokens are decorative), but once this ships an operator cannot tell from a tick log whether the board's numbers came from the local file, the branch, or nothing at all. A persistent miss (mis-typed `tag`, revoked Contents read scope, producer writing to a different repo) is indistinguishable from "producer hasn't landed yet" — both render "—" forever, with zero signal.

The publish path already logs provenance lines:

```js
console.log('  📡 factory state published → ' + spUrl);
```

Consider one sibling line, e.g. `🪙 tokens: N legs (branch|local|none)` — it makes the fallback path observable in the same place, costs nothing per tick, and would have made the gh-781 owner report ("no tokens visible") diagnosable in one glance. Avoid a per-miss `console.warn`: pre-producer the branch 404s every tick and the log would just fill with noise.

Not blocking — purely operability polish.

---

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: gh-781 lands exactly what the ticket scopes — `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch` mirrors `fetchPreviousState` (one gh Contents probe, any miss → `null`), the `readTokensFile || fetchTokensFromBranch` precedence is pinned and tested, and the `tokensMapOf` extraction is a semantics-preserving refactor. Verified locally: `run_factoryState.json` 66/0, `run_smAgent.json` 336/0, full `run_all.json` 1793 passed / 0 failed (matches the PR claim), snapshot schema stays 2; AC1–AC4 each have a dedicated test. No blocking or important findings; security surface is unchanged (repo/tag are config-controlled, gh-first whitelist respected, board-side `esc()` covers the new row fields).

**Key Issues** (all 💡 suggestions, none blocking):
- Fixed `fa-tokens.json` asset vs the documented multi-factory "one branch, one asset per factory" topology — two factories on one branch would cross-attach each other's token rows (ticket pins the name; add a `tokensAsset` knob when a second factory shares a branch)
- Third copy of the gh contents-probe pattern (`fetchPreviousState`, `publishFactoryState`, `updateHistory` ×2) — a shared `contentsOf()` helper would pin the transport in one place
- Tokens source (local/branch/none) is invisible in the tick log — a one-line `🪙 tokens: N legs (<source>)` next to the 📡 publish line would make degradation diagnosable

# pr-783: gh-781 [ENH] Factory board token spend: tick fetches factory-published per-leg token usage (data/fa-tokens.json)

## Description

Closes #781
### What changed
The SM tick's factory state publish now sources per-leg token usage from the `factory-data` branch (`data/fa-tokens.json`) when the local tokens file yields nothing, completing the token pipeline the moment the leg-side producer lands. `card.tokens` feeding is unchanged board-side.

### Key decisions
- New `factoryState.fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg, exec)` mirrors `fetchPreviousState`: one `gh api .../contents/data/fa-tokens.json?ref=<tag> --jq .content | base64 -d` probe; returns `null` on any miss (404, invalid JSON, non-map, rate limit) — tokens stay decorative, the tick never fails on them
- Extracted `tokensMapOf` — one shape contract (array-valued map keyed `pr-N`/`issue-N`) shared by the local-file reader and the branch fetcher; rows still normalize through the existing `normalizeTokens`
- Precedence pinned at the `smAgent.js` statePublish block: `readTokensFile(...) || fetchTokensFromBranch(...)` — local file first (pack-carrying factories keep working), branch fallback, never both
- Branch tag rides `tagOf(cfg)`, so multi-factory `statePublish.tag` overrides apply to the tokens probe too

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json   # new fetchTokensFromBranch suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # AC1–AC3 harness (publish → tokens on cards)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # REG: 1793 passed, 0 failed, schema stays 2
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[SM tick statePublish] --> LOCAL{local tokens file?}
  LOCAL -->|map found| ROWS[rows → card.tokens]
  LOCAL -->|null| GH["gh api …/data/fa-tokens.json @ factory-data"]
  GH -->|valid map| ROWS
  GH -->|404 / garbage / non-map| NONE[token-less cards — tick green]
```

</details>
